milestone.title: Post-RC agent automation — code-review lessons runner, planner agent, hunk integration, dogfood audit, TUI/CLI state parity

intent.outcome: After this ships, M99's runnable Pattern: blocks exist for the L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 code-review lessons; a dedicated mp-planner agent (full read + mp, optimized for planning runs) is installable via mp install --agents; MP-COMMANDS.md command tables are generated from clap definitions with optional snippet includes; a hunk sidecar renderer surfaces mp findings inline in hunk's diff viewer; the M110 S5 dogfood-log audit is shipped as a one-shot review of every dogfood-log entry since the last audit; the docs/code-review-lessons.md runnable code-review-agent skill (mp-code-review) is installable alongside the narrative lessons; and TUI/CLI spec/exec state is verified end-to-end post-M100 migration to close any remaining divergence.

problem.description: Post-RC tail of agent-automation work has been deferred. M99's runnable Pattern: blocks for the L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 lessons were never authored — only the narrative lessons shipped, leaving the runnable pre-screen deferred. A planning-only agent profile would be sharper than the current mp-coordinator/mp-runner pair, which covers execution well. MP-COMMANDS.md drifts from the CLI surface on every clap change; clap-derived command tables with optional snippet includes would close the drift. hunk supports --agent-context for inline diff annotations but the sidecar contract needs an mp adapter. The M110 S5 dogfood-log audit was deferred as a one-shot review pass. The TUI/CLI spec/exec state divergence from the M100 migration left legacy spec_status/execution_status reads in some raul render paths that the unified lifecycle field should now own.

in_scope: Author runnable Pattern: blocks in docs/code-review-lessons.md for L6 (sort-by-id string-cmp), L8 (effective_* helpers vs direct field reads), L13 (cycle detection), L14 (test-name does what name says), L15 (--force is recorded debt). Each block carries the pattern, a positive fixture (must match), and a negative fixture (must not match). Add crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs with grep/ripgrep-driven checks.

Author a dedicated mp-planner agent profile — templates/harness/opencode/agents/mp-planner.md + templates/harness/cursor/agents/mp-planner.md. Profile: read-only mp command set (show, list, search, brief, interview, plan, validate) + agent role 'planning'. Installable via 'mp install --agents=mp-planner'. Pin with an install test.

Add 'mp docgen' command that walks the clap Command tree, emits markdown tables for each subcommand (description, usage, options), and supports optional '<!-- mp:include <fragment> -->' snippet includes in MP-COMMANDS.md / AGENT-READINESS.md. The generator emits a single canonical doc bundle under docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/ that the human-maintained MP-COMMANDS.md includes from.

Add 'mp review sidecar <milestone> [--finding F-XX]' command that writes a JSON sidecar at the path hunk expects (hunk --agent-context <path>), shaped per hunk's agent-context contract. The sidecar lists findings with anchor.path/anchor.line/file/severity/summary; hunk renders them as inline annotations. Wire into mp reviews pass and mp milestone complete flows.

Ship a one-shot M110 S5 dogfood-log audit — review every entry in mp-dogfood-log.md since the M110 ship (entries 22+), triage each as wontfix / backlog / spec-gap / bug / doc. Output: a triage table in docs/dogfood/M110-s5-audit.md with one row per entry and a follow-up backlog promotion for any open items.

Ship the mp-code-review skill — author SKILL.md at templates/skills/mp-code-review/ (parallel to mp-coordinator/mp-runner/mp-flow), and the runnable pattern code (per M99) lives in crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs. Installable via 'mp install --skills=mp-code-review'. The skill's body embeds the lessons catalog from docs/code-review-lessons.md so a reviewer without repo access can still run it.

Audit every spec_status / execution_status read in crates/raul/src/ and route them through effective_spec_status / effective_execution_status helpers (already in crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs). Pin with a parity test that diffs the TUI render badge against 'mp show milestone --fields milestone.lifecycle'.
Run the canonical lint gate: cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy --manifest-path Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings. Both must exit 0 after S1–S7.
out_of_scope: Touching mp-coordinator/mp-runner/mp-flow skills — these are settled; mp-planner / mp-code-review are additive.
Replacing the human-maintained MP-COMMANDS.md entirely with generated output — generation-only; the manual prose stays.
Adding new hunk features — only writes the sidecar hunk already understands.
Re-running the bulk lifecycle migration (migrate_plan_lifecycle) — different migration; this is a render-layer audit.
Promoting the audit findings into milestones during this work — the audit produces the triage doc; promotions happen in subsequent milestones.

findings.description:
M173 S1 ships 'runnable' Pattern: blocks in docs/code-review-lessons.md. The deliverables depend on every Lesson L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 block carrying a positive fixture that an agent can copy/paste to verify the pattern. But the four cited run-commands reference:
 - crates/mp/tests/milestone_bulk.rs (file actually lives at crates/mp/tests/suites/milestone_bulk.rs, not auto-discovered as a top-level test target) 
 - test names bulk_set_spec_status_runs_gate, bulk_set_priority_rejects_invalid_once, no_empty_branches_audit, bulk_depends_on_add_skips_cycle_check_in_dry_run, bulk_depends_on_remove_is_noop_when_edge_missing — none of which exist (the suites/milestone_bulk.rs has bulk_set_priority_by_ids, bulk_set_priority_by_where_filter, bulk_set_priority_partial_failure_continues, bulk_set_spec_status_by_ids_and_where, bulk_set_spec_status_blocks_on_gates)
 
 Reproducer: 'cargo nextest run -p mp --test milestone_bulk -E test(/bulk_set_spec_status_runs_gate/) --no-fail-fast' exits with 'error: no test target named `milestone_bulk` in `mp` package'.
 
 AC-01 says: 'each block carries the pattern, a positive fixture (must match), and a negative fixture (must not match)'. The four positive fixtures do not match — they cite a path/test name that doesn't exist. Without runnable fixtures, M99 spec-gap B-80 (runnable Pattern: blocks never authored) is only formally closed; semantically the patterns are non-runnable and a future code-review sub-agent that follows the lessons' run-commands will fail (this reviewer did).
 
 Lesson line numbers: docs/code-review-lessons.md L6 pattern block ~119–134; L8 ~171–187; L13 ~315–330; L14 ~364–380; L15 ~622–646. Skill file templates/skills/mp-code-review/SKILL.md inherits the broken run-commands in its 'Lessons with runnable Pattern: blocks' table.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: L6/L8/L14/L15 Pattern blocks cite nonexistent tests; 'mp --test milestone_bulk' fails

findings.description:
crates/mp/src/commands/docgen.rs:121 emits the Options header as '| Flag | Long | Description |' but lines 136 then emits each data row as '| {cell} | | {help} |' — the second column (Long) is always empty in the rendered markdown. {cell} already concatenates the short and long flags into the first column (e.g. '-g, --global'), so the header's 'Long' column has no data source.
 
 Concrete evidence in the generated files: docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/install.md lines 11-22 show 9 rows of the form '| `--harness` | |  |' with the middle column blank. The table reads as a 3-col header + 2-col body and is misaligned when any markdown renderer (GitHub, hunk, Obsidian) collapses the empty column.
 
 The fix is one of:
 (a) change the header to '| Flag | Description |' (delete the 'Long' column) and update the data row to '| {cell} | {help} |';
 (b) split {cell} into separate short + long columns and emit '| {short} | {long} | {help} |'.
 
 Affects every generated .md file under docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/ (44 files). The M173 S3 deliverable did not visually inspect the output for table shape.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: docgen Options table has 3-column header but only 2 columns of data — generated docs are misaligned

findings.description:
M173 S7 ships new helpers in crates/raul/src/tui/status.rs (effective_lifecycle, effective_execution_status, effective_spec_status). The header comment (lines 7-21) calls them a 'structurally identical' mirror of mp_model::effective_lifecycle_from_legacy / effective_lifecycle, but they are NOT structural mirrors — both the legacy_status→lifecycle tables and the lifecycle→status tables diverge.
 
 Three concrete divergences verified by reading the two implementations side-by-side:
 
 1. exec_to_lifecycle vs mp_model::legacy_execution_status_to_lifecycle:
    - 'blocked':  TUI status.rs:93 maps to 'in-progress';  mp_model maps to 'draft'.
    - 'deferred': TUI status.rs:94 maps to 'approved';     mp_model maps to 'draft'.
    - 'done':     TUI status.rs:95 maps to 'complete';     mp_model maps to 'done'.
 
 2. spec_to_lifecycle vs mp_model::legacy_spec_status_to_lifecycle:
    - 'groomed' is a lifecycle value, never a legacy spec_status.  When called with spec_status='groomed' (possible for mixed-era fixtures), TUI returns 'groomed', mp_model falls through to default 'draft'.
 
 3. effective_spec_status (NEW — no mp_model equivalent; the validate helper at crates/mp/src/validate/plan.rs:894–905 was the only implementation):
    - lifecycle='in-progress' + no spec_status:
        TUI status.rs:178–184 returns 'verified'.
        validate/plan.rs:898     returns 'ready'.
    - lifecycle='groomed' + no spec_status:
        TUI status.rs:179 returns 'groomed'.
        validate/plan.rs:897 returns 'review'.
    - lifecycle='approved' + no spec_status:
        TUI status.rs:180 returns 'verified' (bundled with in-progress/done/...).
        validate/plan.rs:899 returns 'ready'.
    - lifecycle='done'/'self-reviewed'/'reviewed'/'remediation' + no spec_status:
        TUI status.rs:180 returns 'verified'.
        validate/plan.rs:900 returns 'implemented'.
 
 Effect: a TUI badge row that calls effective_spec_status() on a legacy milestone renders 'verified' for most execution states, while a CLI consumer calling the validate helper renders 'ready'/'implemented'. The parity test crates/raul/tests/tui_status_parity.rs does NOT catch this — it only diffs the helper against itself, not against mp show milestone or validate/plan.rs. AC-07's spec text said the parity test should 'diff the TUI render badge against mp show milestone --fields milestone.lifecycle'; the test as written does not honor that contract.
 
 Concrete reproducer: load a milestone with lifecycle='in-progress' and no spec_status, render the detail view, render the rendered cell — TUI shows 'verified'. Run 'mp show milestone --fields milestone.spec_status_effective'  — validate helper returns 'ready'.
 
 Suggested fix: pick one of (a) collapse the TUI mirror's lifecycle-to-spec_status mapping to align with validate/plan.rs; (b) make validate/plan.rs the single source of truth and have the TUI helper call it via the typed model; (c) add a parity test that imports both helpers and diffs them across a fixture matrix covering every (lifecycle, spec_status, exec_status, blocked, deferred, cancelled) tuple.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: TUI status helpers diverge from validate/plan.rs — TUI renders wrong badge for legacy milestones

findings.description:
crates/mp/src/commands/docgen.rs:39-44 + :77-80 default the output directory to std::env::current_dir().join('docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/'). The clap help text in crates/mp/src/cli/mod.rs:434-436 promises: 'Default: <plan_dir>/../docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/ (i.e. <project_root>/docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/)'.
 
 This is the L8 lesson: 'validate op-level args once at dispatch'. The Cli already carries the resolved PlanContext (ctx is passed in unused — '_ctx: &PlanContext'). The default should be derived from ctx.plan_dir (plan_dir.parent() join 'docs/...'), not cwd. As written, an agent invocation  from any directory other than the project root silently lands in the wrong directory; the CLI then runs  skipped, so the wrong-dir failure mode is silent (it appears to succeed if the path is writable).
 
 Fix: replace default_out_dir with a plan_dir-rooted path, or at minimum validate that cwd contains the docs/concepts tree before falling back.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: 'mp docgen' default --out uses cwd, not plan_dir — wrong location for any non-cwd invocation

findings.description:
crates/mp/src/harness.rs:177-188 (resolved_agent_dir) checks two env var keys:
 1. MP_{ID_UPPER_WITH_UNDERSCORES}_AGENT_DIR (e.g. opencode -> MP_OPENCODE_AGENT_DIR, claude-code -> MP_CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT_DIR)
 2. MP_{ID_UPPER}_AGENT_DIR (e.g. opencode -> MP_OPENCODE_AGENT_DIR again; claude-code -> MP_CLAUDE-CODE_AGENT_DIR which contains a hyphen and is not a valid POSIX env-var name)
 
 For non-hyphenated harness ids (opencode, cursor, gemini, pi, ...) the two keys resolve to the same string, making the second branch a duplicate. For hyphenated ids (claude-code) the second branch constructs an invalid env-var name (MP_CLAUDE-CODE_AGENT_DIR has a hyphen), so getenv always returns Err for that branch and it is dead code.
 
 The whole point of the two-branch fallback per the doc comment was to honor a no-underscore env var name, but POSIX env-var names cannot contain hyphens, so the second branch is unreachable. Suggested fix: delete the second branch (lines 184-187) and rely on a single key, or document why the second variant would ever produce a distinct lookup.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: resolved_agent_dir checks two env-var keys; the second is dead code (and invalid for hyphenated harnesses)

findings.description:
templates/skills/mp-code-review/SKILL.md lines ~50-58 builds a 'Lessons with runnable Pattern: blocks (M173 S1)' table. Each row pins the run command from the underlying lesson's positive fixture; those commands are the same broken nextest targets identified in F-03 (--test milestone_bulk does not exist; cited test names do not exist).
 
 When an agent loads the mp-code-review skill and follows the documented 'run command' for L6/L8/L14/L15, the command exits with 'error: no tests to run' or 'error: no test target named milestone_bulk'. The skill advertises these as runnable, but they are not.
 
 Fix: update SKILL.md to point at the actually-existing tests (cargo nextest run -p mp -E test(/bulk_set_spec_status_blocks_on_gates/) --no-fail-fast etc.), or to use the grep-only patterns where no test target exists. Once F-03 is fixed at the lessons file, this skill row will inherit the corrected commands automatically.

crates/mp/src/commands/docgen.rs places 'use anyhow::Context;' on line 145, between the production render_group function and the #[cfg(test)] module. Convention from crates/mp/src/commands/install.rs and crates/mp/src/commands/reviews.rs is to put all imports at the top of the file. This is a stylistic smell (works, but inconsistent with the rest of the codebase) and a dead-code allow signal per the L13 addendum in docs/code-review-lessons.md ('the dead-call shim that creates fake call sites').

findings.description:
M173 AC-07 in master-plan/milestones/173-...json description says 'Pin with a parity test that diffs the TUI render badge against mp show milestone --fields milestone.lifecycle'. 
 The actual parity test at crates/raul/tests/tui_status_parity.rs:63-203 only diffs against the helper's own return value (e.g. line 75-79: 'let expected = effective_lifecycle(&milestone); assert_eq!(expected, ...);'). It never invokes mp show milestone, never cross-checks the tui helper against crates/mp/src/validate/plan.rs::effective_spec_status, and never runs the binary end-to-end.
 
 This is the L62 lesson in reverse: the doc-comment/spec promises 'same X as sibling path', but the assertion surface only pins one path (the helper) and skips the other (the CLI / validate helper). When the helper and the CLI diverge on the same input (see F-04), this test stays green.
 
 Fix: in tui_status_parity.rs, add a test that boots an mp binary against a fixture milestone and diffs 'mp show milestone --fields milestone.lifecycle_effective' / '.spec_status_effective' against effective_lifecycle(&m) and effective_spec_status(&m). Cross-import and diff the tui helper against mp/src/validate/plan.rs::effective_spec_status; cross-diff against mp_model::effective_lifecycle for the lifecycle mirror.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: AC-07 spec text vs test contract drift: test diffs TUI helper against itself, not against mp show milestone

findings.description:
crates/mp/src/commands/reviews.rs:672-680 (cmd_review_sidecar) handles --finding by simply retaining any finding whose id matches: 'findings.retain(|f| f.id == fid);'. It does NOT filter by status (open / fixed / resolved). A milestone with F-01 (open) and F-01 (resolved, e.g. with fixed_in=milestone:175) would include the resolved one in the sidecar without warning.
 
 The intent per the spec (S4: 'mp review sidecar <milestone> [--finding F-XX]' for inline annotations in hunk) is open findings rendered as TODOs; a resolved finding rendered as an annotation is misleading. The dual precedent (mp reviews finding list --status open) shows that the canonical 'open findings' filter is a separate filter that lives outside this command.
 
 Concrete reproducer: write a milestone with two findings sharing id F-01 (one open, one fixed). 'mp review sidecar <id> --finding F-01 --output /tmp/s.json' emits both annotations.
 
 Suggested fix: retain by id AND status==open by default; add --include-resolved if the caller wants both; document the choice in the clap help text.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: mp review sidecar --finding does not filter by status; emits fixed findings

findings.description:
Generated docs/concepts/06 - Reference/generated/install.md:11 shows Options header with bar-pipe alignment: '| Flag | Long | Description |' plus '|------|------|-------------|' (three dashes vs two). Markdown renderers frequently mis-align with mixed dash counts in the separator row. While the underlying bug is the empty middle data column (F-04), this is the relatedly-bad alignment that worsens the visual output: the dashes are all six long, but mixing widths signals 'intentionally trimmable'; this is the same shape of the subcommand tables (which use '------' vs '------' to align both Name and Description as 6-wide).
 
 Note: the more serious bug is the empty middle column (see F-04); this finding is filed separately for awareness, but should be folded into the F-04 fix.
findings.author: mp-code-review-subagent
findings.summary: docgen.rs Options table column-width alignment collapses header column visibility

findings.description:
templates/harness/opencode/agents/mp-planner.md and templates/harness/cursor/agents/mp-planner.md are nearly-identical content (only one text reflow difference on line 16-17: 'Your job / is the planning domain' vs 'Your job is / the planning domain'). The harness spec said each harness should get its own copy that may carry harness-specific metadata; the two files are functionally identical, and the install_preserves_agent_file_bytes test only verifies byte-identical deploy (within one harness), not cross-harness symmetry.
 
 If the design intent is 'one source of truth, per-harness overrides only where needed', the duplicate content risks drift. If the intent is 'each harness gets its own copy', the test should also assert byte-symmetry across harnesses for the same fields and reject the line-break drift.
 
 Fix: either extract a canonical mp-planner.md at templates/harness/_common/agents/mp-planner.md and have per-harness files reference it, or add a test that asserts the front-matter (--, -- names matter for metadata) matches across all copies.

findings.summary: mp-planner template agent files for opencode and cursor differ only in line-break position; not byte-identical

findings.description: M173 external review (round 2): F-03 was marked status=fixed but only L6 was corrected. L8/L14/L15 Pattern blocks in docs/code-review-lessons.md still cite non-resolving commands. (1) L14 (~L378): 'cargo nextest run -p mp --test milestone_bulk -E test(/no_empty_branches_audit/)' -- '--test milestone_bulk' is NOT a valid target (real target is suite_milestone; milestone_bulk is a #[path]-included module), and no_empty_branches_audit exists nowhere. (2) L15 (~L631-638): wrong path 'crates/mp/tests/milestone_bulk.rs' (actual tests/suites/milestone_bulk.rs), four nonexistent test names (bulk_set_spec_status_runs_gate / bulk_set_priority_rejects_invalid_once / bulk_depends_on_add_skips_cycle_check_in_dry_run / bulk_depends_on_remove_is_noop_when_edge_missing), invalid '--test milestone_bulk'. (3) L8 (~L183): vague 'cargo nextest run -p mp -E test(/milestone_bulk/)' overclaiming an unpinned 'per-priority rejection test'. Reproducer: 'cargo nextest run -p mp --test milestone_bulk' => no test target named milestone_bulk. Defeats AC-01 runnable-fixture contract.

M173 external review (round 2): the runnable-fixture gate crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs::pattern_blocks_contain_runnable_commands (T-04) is purely syntactic -- it only asserts each Pattern block contains a token starting with cargo /rg /make /git /bash . It never validates a cited --test <TARGET> resolves to a real test target nor that a test(/NAME/) filter names a real test. That is why the broken L8/L14/L15 commands (F-16) passed CI: --test milestone_bulk starts with cargo-adjacent tokens so T-04 stayed green. L1 (green tests != correct behavior) in the repo own gate. Fix: add a gate resolving every --test <T> (scoped to -p mp) against crates/mp/tests/<T>.rs and every plain-identifier test(/NAME/) against the tests tree.
